transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My mind keeps getting stuck on the same upsetting thoughts about messing things up for my family and at work, and I can’t let them go. It just feels like I'm constantly trapped in my own head, and it's becoming really exhausting.

When these upsetting thoughts come up, do you feel driven to do anything over and over—like checking, repeating, counting, or seeking reassurance—to make the anxiety go down? Or are they more like constant worries without any rituals?

Yes, I definitely feel driven to do repetitive things to calm myself down. I end up rereading emails, medical notes, and server configs three or four times, or silently running through mental checklists. I just can't move on to the next task until everything feels "just right."

Do these thoughts feel intrusive and irrational—like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them—or are they mostly worries about real-life problems that feel hard to control? Also, are the repetitive checking and mental reviews mainly to neutralize the anxiety from those thoughts?

Yes, they feel incredibly intrusive and irrational; even though they start with real-life duties like my sister's care or my job, they quickly spiral into overwhelming "what-if" scenarios that I can't stop. The repetitive checking and mental checklists are done specifically to quiet that intense anxiety and get things to feel "just right" so I can finally move on.
When you’re in the middle of these thoughts and checking rituals, do you recognize that they’re probably excessive or unreasonable, or do they feel completely true and justified at the time?

Intellectually, I know these thoughts are irrational and that all this constant checking is excessive and a waste of time. But in the heat of the moment, the anxiety feels so incredibly real and overwhelming that I feel like I absolutely have to perform these rituals until everything feels "just right" before I can move on.
About how much time do these obsessions and checking rituals take up in a typical day, and how much are they interfering with your work or daily life?

These thoughts and rituals easily consume several hours of my day and often keep me lying awake for hours at night. It's severely interfering with my life; I've started missing critical details at work and have had to step back from mentoring youth, community events, and hobbies like hiking and drumming because I'm just too mentally exhausted.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent intrusive, irrational obsessions centered on harm/responsibility, along with compulsive checking and mental rituals performed to reduce anxiety and achieve a 'just right' feeling. The patient has preserved insight, symptoms consume several hours daily, and there is clear functional impairment in work, sleep, and social/volunteer activities. This is most consistent with predominantly obsessional thoughts or ruminations within obsessive-compulsive disorder.
